<content>
Status: PROPOSED FOR P23 / HISTORY OWNER ACCEPTANCE. Not Current Authority until explicitly accepted and linked from the authoritative D07 record. This candidate does not authorize implementation.

## Triggering evidence

The execution owner reports a D07 audit on the Selection Batch 3 worktree:

- Product baseline: codex/selection-summary-batch3 @ c7f874395d55952e9d5288e2a336a21747f37f11
- Audit branch in the same worktree: codex/fc04-d07-selection-audit
- Audit result commit: e02fb7b8601bd01be968dbfb6aa783cfb3027e25
- Regression suite: 160 passed
- D07 audit: 11 passed, 3 failed
- Report: local worktree file .aegis/results/FC04-D07-AUDIT/[report.md](http://report.md)
- Commands: local worktree file .aegis/results/FC04-D07-AUDIT/commands.json
- Reported unresolved areas: cross-Operation coordination, one user-visible Undo unit, and post-commit memory-failure handling.

These revision/file identities are supplied by the execution owner. The local C: paths and audit commit were not accessible through the connected GitHub repository surface during this control review; the P23 owner/Codex must read and bind the exact local report and commands before accepting this amendment.

## User-visible product requirement

One user intent that requires multiple canonical Operations must:

1. commit as one coherent local user-visible result and create exactly one user-visible Undo unit; or
2. fail before any canonical mutation and create no successful History item.

No UI may present several independently committed operations as one atomic user intent.

## Proposed minimum local guarantee

This amendment concerns one local Runtime command and its local Scene/History observers. It does not claim crash-atomic persistence, cross-client atomic visibility, distributed transactions, or a new wire-level Transaction.

Before the first canonical mutation:

- Resolve a coherent SelectionContext and normalized operation roots.
- Validate all target states and all forward Operations against the same admitted intent context.
- Construct every required inverse/preimage and expectation.
- Reserve HistoryGroup/UndoIntent capacity and any receipt/result/publication storage needed after commit.
- Ensure no fallible allocation or unhandled exception can occur after canonical mutation begins unless the accepted commit path contains it without partial observable state.

Commit:

- Use the existing IntentPlan / IntentCommitSegment / UndoIntent / HistoryGroup owners and ordinary typed Operations.
- Serialize the local commit segment so no partial Scene/observer publication escapes between constituent operations.
- Preserve ordinary operation identities, semantic validation and per-operation records as required by the existing contract; do not add a canonical global Transaction object or arbitrary wire-level operation list.
- Publish the final coherent local result only after all required forward operations succeed and the one user-visible HistoryGroup is ready to commit.

Failure:

- A precommit failure leaves Document, Scene/index publication, History cursor and redo branch unchanged.
- If an internal apply can fail after mutation begins, it must be prevented by staged/preflight design or contained within the same serialized segment before publication. Compensation is not automatically proof of atomicity if intermediate ChangeSets/generations/events were externally observable.
- Memory allocation required for HistoryGroup/result publication must be reserved before canonical mutation. If reservation fails, reject before mutation.
- A failed intent creates no successful user-visible Undo item. Any failure path that can leave partial canonical state or a visible intermediate publication is a blocker and must be repaired or explicitly re-authorized.

Undo/Redo:

- One successful intent yields one user-visible Undo unit.
- Undo targets the exact committed operations/preimages captured at commit, not the current selection.
- Redo replays the accepted forward intent with fresh operation identities according to current History rules.
- Rejected/failed intents do not advance the History cursor or destroy the redo branch.

## Authority boundaries

- This is a targeted D07 request. It does not resolve D06-B eligible-subset policy; D06-B remains separately governed by its own request.
- Existing 07-14 contract remains authoritative until a replacement/amendment is accepted. If its per-operation publication semantics conflict with the proposed local no-intermediate-publication guarantee, the owner must explicitly reconcile that conflict; implementation may not silently override it.
- No new canonical Transaction, OperationKind, FieldId, ObjectKind, global registry, or public ABI is authorized by this amendment.
- No cross-client/crash atomicity requirement is added.

## Required verification

Bind to the exact D07 audit test names and commands from [report.md/commands.json](http://report.md/commands.json), then ensure the previously failing cases are fixed. Required properties include:

- all-forward preflight before first mutation;
- HistoryGroup and inverse/result memory reservation before mutation;
- successful multi-operation intent produces exactly one user-visible Undo unit;
- injected failure at each operation boundary does not expose a partial local Scene/observer state;
- post-commit memory failure cannot strand canonical state without a History item;
- Undo after changing selection restores the original targets;
- Redo preserves forward meaning and cursor behavior;
- failed intent preserves Document snapshot, Scene/index publication, generation/event semantics allowed by accepted contract, History cursor and redo branch;
- all 160 existing Selection regressions remain passing.

The 160 regression passes are corroborative baseline evidence, not proof of D07 closure. The 11 passing D07 checks must remain recorded; do not weaken or delete them.

## Acceptance requested

P23 / History owner must:

- accept this minimum local guarantee as a targeted D07 amendment; or
- amend the wording to match an existing accepted contract; or
- return the exact incompatible clause and required product decision.

After acceptance, a separately materialized P31 repair package may authorize the narrow D07 code/test repair. Until then, this page is a candidate and product implementation remains unauthorized.
